SmartKem slips 10%, announces 1-for-5 reverse stock split
data.description:
• SmartKem (SMTK) board of directors approved a 1-for-5 reverse stock split of its common stock as the company seeks to support its continued Nasdaq listing.
  • The reverse stock split will become effective on November 20, 2026, at 5 p.m. ET, with shares beginning split-adjusted trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market at the opening of trading on November 23 under the existing ticker symbol SMTK.
  • The stock price slipped about 10% on Thursday pre-market trade.

data.title: Aurania announces non-brokered private placement of up to C$2M
data.description:
• Aurania Resources (ARU:CA) (AUIAF) on Thursday announced its intention to complete a non-brokered private placement financing of up to 10M units of the company at a price of C$0.20 per unit for aggregate gross proceeds to the company of up to C$2M.
  • The company has reserved the right to increase the size of the offering by up to 25% of the size of the offering, such that up to an additional 2.5M units may be issued to raise additional gross proceeds of up to C$500,000.
  • Each unit will consist of one common share of the company and one common share purchase warrant. Each warrant will entitle the holder to purchase one common share at an exercise price of C$0.50 per warrant share for a period of 36 months following the closing of the offering.
  • The company intends to use the net proceeds from the offering for exploration at the company's mineral properties and for working capital purposes.
  • Closing of the offering is anticipated to be completed on or about December 9.
  • Certain directors and officers of the company are expected to acquire units under the offering. 
  • Press release

data.title: Nvidia Quant rating cut to Hold from Strong Buy as momentum weakens
data.description:
Nvidia’s (NVDA) Seeking Alpha Quant rating was downgraded from Strong Buy to Hold on Thursday, as weakening share-price momentum dragged down its overall quantitative score. 

The chipmaker’s Quant Score fell 1.44 points, from 4.92 to 3.48, while its Momentum grade deteriorated from C- to D+. 

The downgrade has also left Nvidia at the bottom of a comparison of its peer semiconductor stocks, with other companies in the screen carrying either Buy or Strong Buy ratings. The shift highlights a growing disconnect between Nvidia’s strong operating performance and its weakening market momentum amid leadership uncertainty.

The downgrade came despite Nvidia shares rebounding 2.29% between November 18 and 19, from $150.96 to $154.41. The stock has nevertheless faced considerable selling pressure in November, with its decline extending to around 36% from its October record.

Its weakening technical profile has contrasted with its still-strong fundamental factor grades: Growth and Profitability both remained at A+, Valuation improved from B+ to A-, and EPS Revisions held at B-.

The Momentum grade, however, fell to D+, weighing heavily on the overall rating. Seeking Alpha's Quant framework evaluates stocks across factors including value, growth, profitability, momentum and earnings revisions, with ratings also taking account of relative performance against peers.

The deterioration in sentiment has unfolded alongside an unsettled leadership transition. Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO on November 12, with CFO Colette Kress taking over as interim chief executive while the board searches for a permanent successor.

The board has indicated that it does not intend to reinstate Huang, despite calls from some investors for his return. The transition has added uncertainty for shareholders given Huang's central role in Nvidia's strategy and its position in the artificial intelligence market.

Nvidia's latest quarterly results, meanwhile, remained exceptionally strong. For fiscal third-quarter 2027, revenue surged 103% year over year to $115.84 billion, exceeding analyst expectations of $109.33 billion, while adjusted earnings of $2.68 per share topped estimates of $2.48.

The contrast between Nvidia's earnings performance and its relative Quant standing is becoming increasingly pronounced. While the company's A+ Growth and Profitability grades point to continued fundamental strength, its D+ Momentum grade and 3.48 overall score have pushed it below the other nine semiconductor stocks in the comparison.

Seeking Alpha's Quant Ratings system grades stocks on their relative performance on key quantitative metrics. It hones in on stocks with the strongest combination of value, growth, profitability, EPS revisions and price momentum relative to their sector peers. data.title: Gamers dive into Grand Theft Auto 6 after the long wait
data.description:
Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) successfully launched Grand Theft Auto 6 late Wednesday night and into Thursday across time zones around the world. Sensor Tower estimated advance sales of GTA 6 to top 17M, with 75% of the sales estimated to be on Sony (SONY) PlayStation consoles. The debut of the game is also reported to have broken livestream records on Twitch (AMZN) and YouTube (GOOG) (GOOGL).

For the company, the release ended a bumpy road to bringing the franchise back after a 13-year absence. However, GTA 6 landed the highest consensus rating ever with critics, which bodes well for Take-Two (TTWO) matching or exceeding its revenue guidance.

"Grand Theft Auto VI represents everything we have been working towards since we first started making games," updated Rockstar Games founder Sam Houser. "Whether you can trace your journey to this game through the entire series or are experiencing Grand Theft Auto for the first time, we hope that we have created an experience that exceeds your expectations for what’s possible from this medium," he added.

Shares of Take-Two (TTW) fell 4.4% in premarket trading after rising 6.2% on Wednesday. Wall Street analysts have a consensus Buy rating on the stock, while Seeking Alpha analysts are more cautious with a consensus Hold rating.

data.title: Ryman Hospitality plans $305M Gaylord Rockies expansion
data.description:
• Ryman Hospitality Properties (RHP) plans to add 450 guest rooms, a luxury indoor water experience and a multi-story parking structure to its Gaylord Rockies Resort & Convention Center in Aurora, Colorado.
  • The planned expansion will increase the resort’s guest rooms to 1,951, making it the third-largest Gaylord Hotels property by room count.

data.title: Wallbox sells ABL connectivity unit in deal with Famatel
data.description:
• Wallbox (WBX) sold ABL GmbH's Connectivity business to Famatel, as the EV charging company continues to streamline its operations and focus on its core business.
  • The transaction includes the transfer of the business's assets, proprietary technologies, products and operations, along with employees assigned to the unit. It also includes the shares of ABL Morocco S.A., a subsidiary located in Tangier, Morocco, which will no longer be part of the Wallbox Group.
  • ABL's eMobility business, including its EV charging product portfolio, will remain part of Wallbox.
  • The agreement was signed and the transaction closed on November 16, 2026.
  • The stock price increased about 4% on Thursday pre-market trade.

data.title: Redwire awarded $15M solar array contract from AscendArc
data.description:
• Redwire (RDW) on Thursday said it was awarded an approximately $15 million contract to deliver its Extensible Low-Profile Solar Array wings to AscendArc, a developer of geosynchronous satellites, in Q3 FY2026. 
  • The ELSA wings will be used to power AscendArc’s GEO communications stackable satellite. 
  • Press release

data.title: Coherent stock jumps on $2B share buyback plan
data.description:
• Coherent (COHR) has authorized a $2B share repurchase program, allowing the company to buy back its common stock through open-market purchases, negotiated transactions, accelerated buybacks, block trades, Rule 10b5-1 plans, put options and other derivative transactions.
  • The program has no expiration date and does not obligate Coherent to repurchase any specific number of shares.
  • Shares rose 7% premarket to $228.
